slides.headline: "Sell in May" would have {halved} your gains

slides.title: The myth
paras: The saying: stocks do better from <g>Halloween to May</g>, so sell in May and come back on Oct 31.
Over 30 years of the S&P 500, winters really did gain more on average.
slides.source: Hotcoin calc. from Yahoo Finance monthly closes

slides.title: Year by year
paras: Winters won in some years, summers in others. In 2025 the summer made <g>+22.8%</g>.
slides.source: Yahoo Finance (^GSPC), month-end closes; Nov-Apr runs into the next year

slides.title: Summers still made money
paras: The S&P 500 rose in <g>21 of 30</g> summers.
The worst was 2008, <r>-30%</r>. Most years, sitting out meant missing gains.
slides.source: Hotcoin calc. from Yahoo Finance monthly closes

slides.title: The real test
paras: $1,000 from Oct 1996 to Apr 2026: hold all year, or only from Halloween to May.
Selling every May left you with about <r>half</r>.
slides.source: Hotcoin calc., price only, no dividends, cash earns 0% while out

slides.title: What it means
paras: A pattern can be real and <u>still not worth trading</u>.
Time in the market beat timing the market, again.
slides.source: Past performance doesn't predict future returns. Not financial advice.
